Retain a provisional no-entry stance, preserve the forecasts and original memo, and obtain those missing comparisons before the 30 November checkpoint. changed_sections.new_evidence: The issuer’s current consolidated comparative table reports headline 15–90-day overdue loans at 4.9% versus 4.3% in Q3 2025 and 90+ overdue loans at 7.3% versus 6.7%; both rose 60 basis points year on year. On that issuer-presented comparison, the stable-credit condition attached to the EPS stock-bullish trigger is not met. This does not require treating unavailable credit-cost or allowance comparisons as adverse. Reported risk-adjusted NIM improved from 10.8% to 12.1%, or 130 basis points year on year, despite falling 30 basis points sequentially from 12.4%. Excluding non-recurring items, it rose from 11.9% to 12.7%, or 80 basis points sequentially. On interest-earning balances, early delinquency improved from 8.2% to 8.0% while 90+ delinquency worsened from 11.6% to 12.1% sequentially. These distinct adjustment and denominator bases do not erase the adverse headline year-on-year delinquency comparison. The available source does not state every inclusion in the headline NPL denominator, and continuity with the legacy Brazil-only series is unproved. The scoped issuer-presented consolidated comparison supports a failed stability condition; it does not prove worsening underwriting across every portfolio, future cohort losses, an earnings-surprise cause or the overall Avoid call.
